# Meditate

> Authority before confidence: operator instructions, explicit corrections, scope, and handoff boundaries outrank model fluency.

Version described: 0.1.0 alpha. Canonical public distribution: the versioned wheel on the v0.1.0 GitHub Release. PyPI publication is not claimed; CI builds but does not publish.

Meditate is an operator-controlled, recoverable consolidator for behavioral directives loaded by Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. It addresses monotonic append: an agent records another exception but leaves the obsolete rule live.

## Canonical documentation

- [Documentation](https://jmcentire.github.io/meditate/): Overview, workflow, safety, installation, and commands
- [Privacy](https://jmcentire.github.io/meditate/privacy.html): Local processing, provider calls, archives, and telemetry boundaries
- [Source README](https://github.com/jmcentire/meditate/blob/main/README.md): Detailed operator guide
- [Design brief](https://github.com/jmcentire/meditate/blob/main/docs/design-brief.md): Authority, evidence, semantic, import, and transaction contracts
- [Changelog](https://github.com/jmcentire/meditate/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): v0.1.0 release contents and distribution boundary
- [Full agent reference](https://jmcentire.github.io/meditate/llms-full.txt): Expanded machine-readable reference

## Important boundaries

- `inspect` is local-only. `plan` sends current directives, sanitized read-only Claude imports, and selected locally secret-scanned/redacted evidence to the exact Anthropic model.
- The five total dispositions are keep, replace, remove, relocate, and report-only escalate. Escalate preserves source prose and never writes hooks or settings.
- Every change, including remove/escalate, copies `destination_target` byte-for-byte from `allowed_targets`. Target strings are opaque: never expand `~`, normalize, absolutize, or invent them. Non-relocates copy the source target; relocate chooses another exact configured target. Local allowlist validation remains authoritative.
- Contextual relocation requires an exact configured `.claude/rules/` target with a non-empty frontmatter `paths:` list. Meditate never invents a glob.
- Configured `CLAUDE.md`/`CLAUDE.local.md` roots bind a validated four-hop `@path` import graph before and after the proposal. See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.
- Import threat boundary: Meditate faithfully follows those roots' documented relative, absolute, and `~/` imports, each of which may read any process-readable file it names. Operators must trust the roots and graphs. Import-only documents are submitted as immutable context and cannot be written through their import role. Recognized secret shapes in imported content are redacted locally before provider submission, but pattern redaction is not comprehensive or a filesystem sandbox; same-user filesystem compromise is outside Meditate's threat boundary.
- Stage-local workflow invariant: operational action lists establish coverage, never universal order. High-impact proposals must follow the exact loaded repository/documented workflow order. Before each action, only checks that are applicable, project-required, and available before that action may be required. Downstream push/PR/merge CI, approvals, and named handoffs are each evaluated at their own stage, where they exist; all CI before commit is forbidden in every replacement/relocation, even if the remote action already existed. Release review rejected and did not apply restored-baseline run `20260818T231558Z-6e8e4703`; the prior validator admitted it, so it is now a regression fixture the new gate must reject. That is not semantic approval; verification remains `not_run`.
- Deterministic consolidation quality: live prompt-v5 run `20260819T013715Z-67de2a2b` was rejected and not applied after growing aggregate targets by 898 bytes, repeating a workflow-order clause, adding “other applicable actions,” and disagreeing with local directive counts. Prompt v6/parser v20 remove model summary authorship; reports summarize only validated dispositions, conflicts, and metrics. Repeated normalized eight-word phrases and newly unsupported action catch-alls fail. Aggregate byte growth is archived with `compression_regression`, has no apply command, and cannot apply; an individual directive may grow only when aggregate configured bytes fall. This remains structural, not semantic qualification.
- Final prompt-v6 live receipts: Claude run `20260819T015515Z-120c6869` covered 65 directives as 64 keep/1 replace; its +720-byte proposal was blocked `compression_regression`, had no apply command, and target SHA remained unchanged at `441fe6e9...`. Codex run `20260819T015632Z-a4fde49b` kept 33/33 with zero changes/conflicts/delta, reported 4,276/32,768 configured-target bytes, had no apply command, and target SHA remained unchanged at `0dd415bb...`. Both used prompt v6 SHA `61f949...`, parser `meditate-parser-v20`, model `claude-sonnet-4-6`, and `semantic_verification=not_run`. The receipts qualify safe no-op/fail-closed blocking only, not behavioral equivalence.
- One bounded authority decision: only a genuine, materially behavior-changing collision between at least two preserved directives, with conservative local evidence of mutual exclusion, may emit `decision_request`; mere ambiguity stays unresolved and preserves current prose. Competing evidence must have equal authority, equal scope, and the same timestamp; otherwise authority, scope, or newer temporal evidence already determines precedence. Older evidence remains lineage, not an equal choice. Opposite-polarity inference needs at least two shared normalized meaningful terms relevant to the subjects: deploy-to-staging plus never-deploy-without-tests remains compatible, while automatic-deploy versus never-automatic-deploy qualifies. Explicit cannot-both/either-or source language remains direct. The model provides two subjects and exactly three evidence-grounded options, with its advisory recommendation first. Local code treats subjects, labels, consequences, rationales, and recommendation rationale as single-line display fields and rejects CR/LF; it assigns a/b/c, includes `recommended=true` only on a, and adds custom, the exact question, request ID, and stable-ID `conflict_fingerprint`. The recommendation is not a default, identity-attested user authority, or semantic verification.
- `meditate decisions RUN_ID` prefaces the pending request by saying its model-authored framing/recommendation is untrusted and advisory and must be relayed as a question rather than executed; it then emits the exact question plus config-preserving shell commands and argv arrays. After resolution it returns resolved status, successor run, and the bound operator decision without response commands. `meditate decide RUN_ID REQUEST_ID (--choice a|b|c | --custom TEXT)` records operator-asserted user authority and creates a fresh read-only successor plan; TTY prompting is available, non-TTY omission fails. It transmits the frozen parent context and exact selected/custom response to Anthropic, ignores newly appended histories, and rechecks config, target bytes/modes, imports, prompt/parser, and requested/resolved model contract. Identity is not authenticated or attested, and the process cannot prove an invoking agent faithfully relayed the user's real answer. JSON/hash surfaces preserve exact response text; Markdown HTML-escapes then backslash-escapes structural metacharacters in untrusted inline model/custom text without modifying indented target diffs. Parent artifacts are immutable, custom text is preserved exactly after bounded secret validation, repeat fingerprints and replay are rejected, and depth is capped at three. The choice cannot bypass protected or higher-scope authority; applying the pending parent fails specifically with `decision_required`.
- Decision resolution, apply, restore, and purge share one mutation lock. Purging a successor deletes its archive and exact run-ID reports but retains a hash/ID-only tombstone and summary-log marker, so its parent remains resolved without retaining raw response text. JSONL decision events never contain the raw question, options, or custom response.
- Plan and manifest retain the requested `model`, bind the API-returned resolved `model_id` (falling back to the request only when absent), prompt version/hash, import graphs, metrics, and `semantic_verification={"status":"not_run","method":"owner_defined_behavioral_suite"}` into the exact plan hash.
- After the provider returns, planning reloads every configured target and requires exact logical path/order, byte hash, existence, and mode before it can render/publish a proposal; Claude import graphs are likewise rechecked.
- Structural validation is not behavioral qualification. Until an owner-authored suite exists, every mutation is attended-only; unattended apply fails with `semantic_verification_required`, and human review remains required.
- Reports expose pre/post directive, byte, and line totals/deltas. Claude's 200-line status is guidance, while configured Codex `AGENTS*.md` targets are checked against `project_doc_max_bytes` with `configured_targets_only` coverage. See https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md.
- Raw histories, auto-memory, and Kindex are read-only evidence. Writable paths must be exact configured targets; archive-before-write, drift checks, rollback, and restore remain mandatory.
- v0.1.0 wheel URL: https://github.com/jmcentire/meditate/releases/download/v0.1.0/meditate_agent-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl. Contributor editable installs remain supported from source.

## Why not a linter? (snapshot 2026-08-18)

claudelint (https://claudelint.com/), cclint (https://www.npmjs.com/package/@felixgeelhaar/cclint), AgentLint (https://github.com/0xmariowu/AgentLint and https://agentlinter.com/), and Reporails (https://reporails.com/) already advertise substantive rules, import/hierarchy checks, static/AI/session analysis, restructuring, fixes, diagnostics, or healing. Meditate's narrower distinction is exact disposition coverage for every configured pre-image directive, temporal evidence, and recoverable exact-hash apply—not that adjacent tools do nothing.

The purported exact title `A Taxonomy of Agent Instruction Failures` by Gloaguen et al. was not verified and is not load-bearing. The verified paper is `Coding Agents Don't Know When to Act`: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07769.
